Article Title: Seven CWG golds, one big challenge: Why India's boxing journey is far from over
Article Text:
L-R: Lovlina Borgohain, Jaismine Lamboria, Priya Ghanghas, Preeti Pawar, Sakshi Chaudhary and Arundhati Choudhary at the CWG 2026 in Glasgow. (PTI Photo)

A landmark achievement for Indian boxing

Why Commonwealth success is no longer enough

Asian Games will provide the real verdict

The biggest challenge starts after winning medals

A stronger system is finally delivering results

Devarajan sees echoes of Cuba's golden era

Exposure and depth have changed Indian boxing

The next battle is as much mental as technical

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ten medals - seven gold and three silver. The No. 1 boxing nation at the Commonwealth Games for the first time in history.India's campaign at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow deserves every bit of the celebration it has received. The contingent finished ahead of traditional Commonwealth boxing powers such as England, Australia and Ireland, with the women's team accounting for six of the seven gold medals.Yet, beneath the celebrations lies a bigger question. Has Indian boxing finally reached the level where it can consistently challenge the world's best, or will Glasgow become another memorable Commonwealth Games campaign that fails to translate into sustained success at the Asian Games and the Olympics?For former world champion Laishram Sarita Devi and Olympian-turned-selector Venkatesan Devarajan, Glasgow was never the destination. It was simply the first step towards a much bigger target — proving India's credentials against Asia's finest before taking that momentum into the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.Seven gold medals do not happen by accident. India's dominance reflected years of investment in coaching, sports science, nutrition, overseas exposure and a fiercely competitive domestic circuit. The performance also followed India's encouraging campaign at the 2025 World Championships in Liverpool, where India returned with two golds, one silver and one bronze."It was a historic performance by the boxing team. It was a proud moment for India. We have never achieved such a performance before," Sarita Devi told TimesofIndia.com.The balance of power in amateur boxing has shifted decisively towards Asia. Countries such as Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Chinese Taipei, Japan, DPR Korea and the Philippines have emerged as the sport's dominant forces, consistently producing Olympic and world champions.The numbers underline that shift. Across the last three Olympics, Asian nations have won 16 gold medals compared to just five by Commonwealth countries. Similarly, at the World Championships, excluding India, Asian nations have won 32 world titles, compared to just five by Commonwealth countries.India has been one of the few exceptions, at least at the World Championships, largely due to its consistently successful women's programme, which has produced seven world titles during that period.Even so, Glasgow alone cannot answer the biggest question surrounding Indian boxing: Can India now consistently defeat the very nations that have dominated Olympic boxing over the past decade?If Glasgow showcased India's growing depth, the Asian Games will reveal its true standing among the world's elite.India's recent record explains why the continental event remains the ultimate benchmark.Across the last three Asian Games, Indian boxing has won only two gold medals alongside one silver and eight bronze medals. At the last three Olympics, the country has returned with just one bronze medal.Sarita Devi believes India is steadily narrowing that gap."Asian Games level is higher, but our level is not that bad. We are definitely coming to the levels of other Asian powerhouses like Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China etc. We won so many medals at the World Cup in India too, we are getting better day by day. These powerhouses also fear Indian boxers," she said.But she insists the upcoming Asian Games will determine whether this Indian team has genuinely crossed into the sport's top tier.Sarita Devi believes the toughest task begins after returning home with medals. Managing success, she says, is often harder than chasing it."But we can't just stop after these performances. Other countries are also working hard with their eyes on the next Olympics. In the near future, the Asian Games are just round the corner," she said. "In my opinion, the most important thing now is the recovery path. They just competed in a big massive event, and they have to start preparing for another massive tournament in the Asian Games.""The medallists should remain grounded and keep the fire lit inside like they did when they started at the grassroots level. If we prolonged our celebrations for the CWG success and did not perform at the level we wanted at the Asian Games, the dreams we have from our boxers will not be fulfilled," she added.As a coach herself, Sarita pointed to Commonwealth silver medallist Jadumani Singh Mandengbam, explaining how easily post-Games celebrations can disrupt an athlete's rhythm. "For example, Jadumani will be reaching Manipur on Thursday, and I have to take good care of him as a coach for the next five days, so that he does not lose focus on the game due to excess celebration," she explained."Only after putting up a similar performance in the coming Asian Games with a bigger medal haul than before, we can prove that Indian boxing's level is up to the Asian and world level," she said.Sarita credits improved government support, sports science, nutrition, coaching and overseas exposure for transforming Indian boxing."The Indian government has provided a lot of facilities nowadays regarding sports science, nutrition and good coaches. It has made sure that athletes have all the necessary facilities," she said. "It was different during our times, but now the exposure they got is immense. They got the opportunity to train abroad, exposure of big tournaments."She also credits the increasingly competitive domestic circuit for producing world-class talent across multiple weight divisions."That's the reason why good boxers are coming out from every corner of the country. Since the competition has become intense, those who become No. 1 in the country are also at world level now," she said."BFI hosting big tournaments in India like World Cups gives a lot of motivation to the budding boxers. When we host big tournaments in India with world-class boxers coming to compete here, it motivates the boxers here a lot. It brings a big change," she concluded.Olympian-turned-selector and Arjuna awardee Venkatesan Devarajan believes the investment made in Indian boxing over the last decade and a half is finally paying dividends."Actually this one is really the proud moment of our Indian boxing. Whatever we have done over the last 15 years, now we are getting the benefits," he told TimesofIndia.com.Having recently visited Rohtak, one of India's leading boxing hubs, Devarajan said the training ecosystem reminded him of Cuba."When I was in the 90s... when I visited Cuba... I now see the same infrastructure and the same system in Haryana, Rohtak and nearby Bhiwani," he said. "So many people come and stay outside and do training at Rohtak."For him, perhaps the biggest transformation is that talent is no longer concentrated in a handful of states.Training camps abroad, joint sessions with foreign teams and regular participation in international tournaments have become routine for India's elite boxers — something Devarajan believes has significantly narrowed the gap with the world's best."Before the Commonwealth Games they went to Ireland for training. So that helped so much. Nowadays everyone does combined training... international camps with many countries... that's all a good sign," he said.Another encouraging sign, according to Devarajan, is the depth now available across almost every weight category. Domestic trials have become so competitive that even world champions can no longer take selection for granted."Actually now whatever I'm seeing in India... same like 90s Cuba. First, second and third... no difference," he said proudly.He cited the example of world champion Nikhat Zareen losing at the trials to underline how competitive selection has become."Nikhat Zareen is the world champion, right? That day another girl ( Sakshi Chaudhary ) won the fight," he cited. "Previous performance is not counted. Present performance is very important."Devarajan believes the biggest challenge after Glasgow will be psychological, with success bringing greater expectations. He remains optimistic about India's prospects at the Asian Games."Olympics are important. We will do well in the Asian Games. Two or three gold medals will come," he said."There should not be overconfidence. Mind balance is very important. When victories come, so many people don't know how to balance the mind," he said.He believes experienced coaches, support staff and sports psychologists become invaluable in such situations. His message closely mirrors Sarita Devi's advice that the medal winners must stay grounded and quickly shift their focus to the next challenge.There is little doubt that Indian boxing has entered one of the strongest phases in its history. Better infrastructure, coaching, exposure and domestic competition have produced unprecedented depth, but Glasgow has also raised expectations.If India converts its Commonwealth dominance into Asian titles and consistently beats Asia's best, Glasgow will be remembered as the tournament that marked India's arrival as a genuine global boxing force. If not, it may ultimately be remembered as another outstanding Commonwealth campaign that stopped just short of the sport's highest level.
Article Summary: India won seven gold medals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Commonwealth success is no longer enough for Indian boxing. The Asian Games will reveal India's true standing among the world's elite. The balance of power in amateur boxing has shifted decisively towards Asia.

Article Title: 'We must be ready with every answer': Gautam Gambhir's rallying cry before Sri Lanka Tests
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir (Pic credit: BCCI)

'Make sure we tick all the boxes'

Warm welcome for newcomers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has delivered a rousing message to his young Test squad ahead of the two-match series against Sri Lanka, urging Shubman Gill and his teammates to ensure they are mentally and physically prepared for every challenge from the opening morning in Galle.With the World Test Championship campaign gathering momentum and India looking to climb from fifth in the standings, Gambhir stressed that meticulous preparation over the coming days would determine how the visitors fare in spin-friendly Sri Lankan conditions.The Indian team began training at Colombo's Nondescripts Cricket Club (NCC) ground on Wednesday and will play a three-day warm-up match against a Sri Lanka XI from August 7 to 9 before heading to Galle for the first Test, beginning on August 15. The second Test will be played at Colombo's Sinhalese Sports Club (SSC) from August 23 to 27.Addressing the players in a video shared by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), Gambhir laid down the challenge for the squad."Guys, we know what's in front of us. We know what we are playing for. We can do the volume, we can push our limits, we can tick all the boxes. Come 15th morning, whether we are batting first, or whether we are bowling first, we're absolutely ready with every answer, every question that's thrown at us and every answer we're ready to give.So make sure we tick all the boxes from now on," Gambhir said.The warm-up fixture assumes added importance after India's recent struggles against quality spin bowling. Several frontline batters, including captain Shubman Gill, KL Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal , had already begun working on their game against spin before arriving in Sri Lanka, but the three-day match is expected to provide a crucial taste of local conditions.Many members of the current squad are playing red-ball cricket in Sri Lanka for the first time, with only Rahul, Ravindra Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav having previous Test experience in the island nation.Gambhir also used the team meeting to welcome newcomers Saransh Jain and Auqib Nabi, along with newly appointed fielding coach Subhadeep Ghosh.“Guys, welcome everyone. We've got a couple of new guys in. To start with, Saransh, congratulations, you've worked extremely hard to be here. Make sure that you make your family and country proud whenever you get that opportunity.“Secondly, I want to congratulate Auqib, you had a phenomenal last season, and made J&K win the Ranji Trophy, which is a great achievement. Congratulations once again. Lastly, I want to welcome Joy as well.“He's worked with so many teams for so many years. I'm sure his passion, his commitment will carry this team forward and make sure that his energy levels will help everyone achieve the target, which we want to do,” Gambhir added.India have further strengthened their preparations by drafting in four domestic spinners — Harsh Dubey, Shivang Kumar, Tanush Kotian and Vipraj Nigam — as net bowlers to help the batters sharpen their game against spin.The visitors, however, head into the series with injury concerns. Jasprit Bumrah has been ruled out after failing to recover fully from a knee injury, while Washington Sundar will miss the opening Test with a hamstring issue. Harshit Rana, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Akash Deep are also unavailable.The two-match contest forms part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle, with India currently fifth on the table with a points percentage of 48.150, one place above Sri Lanka, who are sixth with 41.67.
Article Summary: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has delivered a rousing message to his young Test squad ahead of the two-match series against Sri Lanka. The Indian team began training at Colombo's Nondescripts Cricket Club (NCC) ground on Wednesday. India will play a three-day warm-up match against a Sri Lanka XI from August 7 to 9 before heading to Galle for the first Test, beginning on August 15.

Article Title: Ajinkya Rahane on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi: 'IPL and international cricket are completely different'
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Zimbabwe series changes the story

Former India batter Ajinkya Rahane has urged everyone to be patient with young opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, saying it is too early to predict his future in Test cricket. Rahane said the teenager should be allowed to grow, adding that the Indian Premier League and international cricket are "completely different."The 15-year-old Sooryavanshi had a mixed start to his international career. After struggling on his debut tour of England, he bounced back strongly in the T20I series against Zimbabwe, where he finished as the Player of the Series.Speaking on the Stick to Cricket podcast, Rahane said: "It's tough to say or comment on right now. I don't want to say anything and put pressure on that young kid because people are already talking a lot about him. It's just two IPL seasons.""What I've realised is that IPL and international cricket are completely different. The pressure when you represent your country is enormous. Chasing 70 runs in the IPL in four or five overs is easy. Chasing the same number of runs in international cricket is different. So, let him just play his game, let him just grow," he said.Sooryavanshi earned his maiden India call-up after a brilliant IPL 2026 season.Although he was selected for the Ireland and England tours, he did not feature in Ireland. He eventually made his debut in England after Sanju Samson's poor run with the bat.The left-handed batter struggled in his first taste of international cricket, scoring 14, 13 and 15 in three T20Is before losing his place for the final match of the series.Sooryavanshi quickly bounced back from the disappointment of the England tour with a match-winning display against Zimbabwe.He began the three-match T20I series with a half-century, scored 20 in the second game and then blasted 81 off 49 balls in the final match. India completed a 3-0 clean sweep, while the youngster finished with 151 runs at an average of 50.33 to win the Player of the Series award.
Article Summary: Rahane says it is too early to predict Sooryavanshi's future in Test cricket. The 15-year-old has had a mixed start to his international career. He struggled on his debut tour of England but bounced back in the T20I series against Zimbabwe.

Article Title: FIH Women’s Hockey World Cup: Dutch legend Pirmin Blaak fine-tunes goalkeepers Savita, Bichu ahead of India's campaign
Article Text:
Savita training with Pirmin Blaak

Bichu Devi Kharibam (left) and Savita Punia

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With ten days to go before India’s opening match against China at FIH Women’s Hockey World Cup at Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen, the Netherlands, the Indian women’s team is fine-tuning every aspect of its preparation. For goalkeepers Savita Punia and Bichu Devi Kharibam, that has meant learning from one of the best in the business.Former Dutch international goalkeeper — and Paris Olympics men’s gold winner — Pirmin Blaak conducted three specialised goalkeeping sessions with the Indian duo during the team’s recent stint in Germany, where India also played two practice matches. The sessions focused not only on technical aspects but also on the mental side of goalkeeping.According to Savita, the sessions proved invaluable. “It was a very good experience. In fact, better than I had expected,” the veteran goalkeeper told TOI during an exclusive interview from the Netherlands on Wednesday.“We spoke a lot about the mindset a goalkeeper should have, worked on defending drag flicks and discussed mental toughness. His sessions were extremely energetic and high intensity,” she said, “For a goalkeeper, even learning a new small skill can make a huge difference.”Working with the Dutchman had long been part of the plan. Savita revealed that former goalkeeping coach Simon Zijp had earlier told her that if he was unavailable, Pirmin would be the ideal person to continue working with the Indian goalkeepers.Although the duo trained under Pirmin for only three days, Savita believes the quality of the sessions made a significant difference. “There had been a gap since we last had this kind of specialised goalkeeping training. It took us some time to adjust in the first session, but the second and third sessions were really good. He will also be with us during the World Cup,” she said.Bichu, too, said the sessions were built on months of remote guidance from Pirmin, who had been sending training plans and goalkeeping drills to the goalkeepers even before joining them in Germany.“He was unable to come to India, but remained in constant touch,” said the 25-year-old, “He sent us detailed training plans and goalkeeping exercises, which were implemented by our coaches in Bengaluru. We followed those sessions throughout the camp.”Once Pirmin joined them in Germany, however, his influence became first-hand. “He focused on improving our decision-making, explained the best lines to take as a goalkeeper, when to come off the line, how to narrow the angles and how to coordinate better with our defenders,” Bichu added.“A lot of the sessions were about communication between the goalkeeper and the defence — understanding which areas the goalkeeper covers and which areas the defenders should take responsibility for.”Beyond the technical lessons, Bichu is also relishing the prospect of playing another World Cup alongside Savita, whom she credits with playing a significant role in her development.“Savita always tells me that every goalkeeper concedes goals and the important thing is to forget about it quickly and move on,” said Bichu, “That advice has helped me focus much better. If you concede a goal and keep thinking about it, you won’t be able to perform in the next moment.”The admiration is mutual.“I have a lot of confidence in Bichu. She is a very good goalkeeper with a very bright future. One of her biggest qualities is her sincerity. Very few players are as dedicated to improving themselves as she is,” said Savita, who is among six players in the squad set to feature in their third World Cup.Savita, meanwhile, hopes this edition of the World Cup will be India’s best yet. “This is my third World Cup. I want us to achieve something even better than what we managed in the previous two editions,” she said.Armed with fresh inputs from one of Europe’s finest goalkeepers and buoyed by a partnership built on trust and mutual respect, Savita and Bichu now have just one objective — to ensure India’s last line of defence is ready when they play their first match in 10 days’ time.
Article Summary: Savita Punia and Bichu Devi Kharibam trained with former Dutch international goalkeeper Pirmin Blaak. The sessions focused not only on technical aspects but also on the mental side of goalkeeping. India’s opening match against China at FIH Women's Hockey World Cup at Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen.

Article Title: Have learnt to control my nerves in important matches: Divyanshi Bhowmick
Article Text:
Divyanshi Bhowmick (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: At an age when most teenagers are juggling school and exams, 15-year-old Divyanshi Bhowmick is already measuring herself against some of the world’s best table tennis players. Competing at the 22nd Commonwealth Table Tennis Championships in New Delhi, Divyanshi once again underlined why she is regarded as one of India’s brightest prospects. She won the women’s doubles silver alongside Yashaswini Ghorpade.Last year, Divyanshi became the first Indian in 36 years to win the U-15 girls’ singles title at the Asian Youth Table Tennis Championships, beating three Chinese opponents on her way to gold. She followed it up with a historic bronze medal at the World Youth Championships, becoming only the second Indian to finish on the podium at the event. For Divyanshi, though, medals are merely milestones in a much longer journey.“It’s good to have a tournament in India where you can play against such experienced senior players. You learn so much from every match,” she said. “Competing with my seniors is always a great opportunity.”The past year has exposed the teenager to a demanding international calendar, and she believes the biggest gains have come not in technique but temperament.“Playing so many tournaments has helped me control my nerves during crucial matches,” she said. “That’s where I’ve improved most.”Asked who inspired her to take up the sport, the answer came instantly. “Manika Batra,” she said with a smile. “She’s my inspiration.”Regular exposure on the international circuit has also given Divyanshi a firsthand look at the standards set by traditional powerhouses such as China and South Korea. While she feels India has narrowed the gap in recent years, she believes the leading nations continue to hold an edge in physicality.“They have a lot of power and they’re extremely fit. Whenever I play them, they’re always ready to get to every ball,” she said.
Article Summary: Divyanshi Bhowmick is one of India's brightest table tennis prospects. The 15-year-old won the women's doubles silver at the Commonwealth Championships. She is the first Indian in 36 years to win the U-15 girls' singles title.

Article Title: Selection row hits Asian Para Games build-up
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Selection issues have again come to the fore ahead of the Asian Para Games in Japan, with para cyclists and a para shooter raising concerns over eligibility norms and their implementation, prompting legal scrutiny.Para rifle shooter Simran Sharma has approached the Delhi high court , apprehending that she could miss the Games and other international events because of the Minimum Qualification Score (MQS) criteria prescribed under the domestic selection policy. Her petition seeks directions allowing participation in the Aichi-Nagoya Games without mechanically applying the impugned MQS norms.Simran, 17, competes in the SH2 rifle category, meant for athletes who cannot independently support the weight of a rifle and therefore use a spring-supported shooting stand. She was earlier classified in SH1, meant for shooters capable of supporting the firearm without assistance, before her classification was corrected in 2024. The petition states she is currently India No.1 in R4 and R5 and No.2 in R9 in SH2.According to the petition, Simran exceeded the MQS prescribed under the official Games qualification framework during selection trials at Mhow in May. However, she contends that the domestic policy fixed “artificially inflated” or significantly higher benchmarks, including 630.2 against the Games MQS of 615.0 in mixed 10m air rifle standing (R4), 635.4 against 625.0 in mixed 10m air rifle prone (R5), and 620.2 against 600.0 in mixed 50m rifle prone (R9), resulting in her exclusion despite competitive performances.The plea also questions the basis of adopting tougher standards than those prescribed for the Games and those outlined in the govt's selection criteria.Meanwhile, concerns have also been raised in para cycling over the Games qualification process. Athletes have alleged inconsistencies in applying published eligibility criteria, administrative lapses affecting qualification opportunities, repeated policy changes, and lack of transparency in selections. Representations submitted to authorities have sought an independent review, alleging deviations from notified procedures and continued uncertainty surrounding team selection before the continental event.
Article Summary: Para rifle shooter Simran Sharma has approached the Delhi high court. She fears she could miss the Games and other international events because of the Minimum Qualification Score (MQS) criteria. Concerns have also been raised in para cycling over the Games qualification process.

Article Title: BWF World Championships draw: Ayush Shetty handed tough test against world No. 1 Shi Yu Qi in opener
Article Text:
Ayush Shetty

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The road to a home World Championships podium could hardly be tougher for rising star Ayush Shetty after the BWF World Championships draw, announced here on Wednesday, pitched the unseeded Indian against defending champion, top seed and World No. 1 Shi Yu Qi of China in a riveting opening round clash. The tournament will be held at the IGI Stadium from Aug 17 to 23.Ayush, who lost to Shi in this year’s Badminton Asia Championships final, gets an opportunity to avenge that defeat. Chief national coach Pullela Gopichand felt the daunting opener could yet work in the youngster’s favour. “I do believe Ayush is very good and with his attacking style, playing Shi in the first round is better than meeting him later. If he wins, it opens up the draw,” Gopichand said, adding, “Overall, it looks like a good draw from the Indian perspective. We aspire to end up on the podium in a few events.”Former champion (2019) PV Sindhu , seeded ninth, has landed in the lower quarter of the women’s top half, ensuring she won’t meet World No. 1 South Korean An Se Young before the semifinals. Fresh from her Japan Open triumph, Sindhu could face China’s Wang Zhi Yi in the pre-quarter, Indonesia’s Putri Kusuma Wardani in the last eight and Se Young in the semis. Lakshya Sen , bronze medallist in 2021, and seeded 14th this time, appears to have a decent route to the Round of 16. He could run into Thailand’s Kunlavut Vitidsarn in the pre-quarters, French duo of Christo Popov or Alex Lanier in the quarters, with Singapore’s Loh Kean Yew or Victor Lai of Canada potential semis opponents.Fifth-seed Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty headline India’s doubles hopes and are projected to meet Indonesian pairing of Raymond Indra-Nikolaus Joaquin and Fajar Alfian-Muhammad Shohibul Fikri and China’s Liang Wei Keng-Wang Chang en route to the final, while avoiding defending champions, South Korea’s Seo Seung Jae-Kim Won Ho, and Malaysia’s Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik until the title clash.Men’s doubles coach Tan Kim Her said Satwik has recovered well from the recurring shoulder injury that forced the pair to withdraw from the Japan Open and entirely skip the China Open. “His rehabilitation has gone well. He has recovered and is fit to take the court,” he said.In women’s doubles, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand open against Spain’s Paula Lopez and Lucia Rodriguez. Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto, 15th seed, will lead the country’s charge in the mixed doubles.Badminton World Federation’s (BWF) Events Director, Selvaamresh Supramaniam, praised extensive renovations at the venue, saying shortcomings flagged after the India Open in Jan this year had “largely been addressed”.“The last three days that I have been there, I didn’t see any pigeons. I didn’t see any monkeys. They have finished putting gel on the roof. This gel prevents birds from sitting or perching on the beams,” Supramaniam said.
Article Summary: Ayush Shetty to play Shi Yu Qi of China in opening round of World Championships. PV Sindhu lands in lower quarter of women's top half. Lakshya Sen appears to have a decent route to Round of 16. Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty headline India’s doubles hopes.

Article Title: FC1 out to build football’s future in J&K and Ladakh
Article Text:
(Pic credit: TOI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: Not long ago, Real Kashmir FC introduced Indian football enthusiasts to the love for football in Jammu & Kashmir. Last year, 1 Ladakh FC made its debut in the Durand Cup and brought its message of climate change to the Indian mainland.This time, at 135th edition of Asia’s oldest football tournament, there’s a club from the northern Himalayan region of the country – combining the love for football in the region with its philosophy of conservation – in its bid to create a platform for players from Jammu & Kashmir as well as Ladakh through FC1.“We are not here to compete with anyone or copy someone’s journey. We have a different mission. We are building a development club focused on grassroots football, sustainability and long-term results,” FC1 CEO Jehad Shona, who was also involved with the founding of Real Kashmir, told TOI.“Our responsibility is to find talent across Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh, give young players a serious platform, and prepare them for the highest level. We are working towards a future in which players from this region can compete for places at 2034 FIFA World Cup and 2036 Olympic Games.”While that dream may still be miles away, their long journey to the Assam capital for their first major tournament has already reaped dividends as they made a winning debut in Durand Cup with a 1-0 victory over Karbi Anglong Morning Star FC in Guwahati on Monday.“For me, the most important fact is what happened in our victory on Aug 3. We had 10 local players on the field, playing together and winning FC1’s debut match,” explained Shona.That's really what Durand Cup is for one of its new competitors — a chance to test themselves against clubs with far more history, in a tournament that doesn’t hand out easy games.Being drawn in Group F, alongside defending champions NorthEast United FC, Morning Star and their next opponents in the tournament on Thursday, Bodoland FC, they are grouped with an established ISL side and two more of the region’s grassroots-driven clubs.“The journey was good. We had a good three weeks of preparation before travelling to Guwahati for our matches,” head coach Khalid Qayoom told TOI from Guwahati.Their Durand Cup squad includes Ilyas and Rahula from Ladakh, and Nirdosh from Jammu. Coach Khalid Qayoom and several other players are from Kashmir, while the squad also features two foreigners, Lacine Diakite and Tetty Armando Yoko.There’s also an environmental cause attached to their debut.FC1 has dedicated its first season to water conservation and teamed up with PUMA on a jersey built around that theme — clean lines to evoke water’s movement and purity, a way of using the shirt to start conversations that go beyond the 90 minutes.For now, however, they have shone in their first 90 minutes on the pitch.“As captain, I’m incredibly proud of the effort and character shown by every player,” skipper Ikhlaq said of their first win.“We worked hard during our three weeks of preparation, and that unity was evident on the pitch. Even after going down to 10 men for more than 30 minutes, the team never stopped believing.“Everyone fought for each other, stayed disciplined, and showed tremendous resilience to grind out the result. Performances like this build confidence, strengthen our bond as a team, and provide the perfect platform for the matches ahead,” he added.That bond is also part of the name. The '1' in it is meant to signal one crest, one team, pulled together from three regions that don’t always get to share a spotlight.“People can discuss names, regions and nationalities. I look at performance. Ten local players performed, ten local players showed character, and FC1 won. That tells you everything about the direction of this club,” was how Shona put it in conclusion.
Article Summary: 1 Ladakh FC makes its debut in Durand Cup. Club combines love for football in Jammu & Kashmir with philosophy of conservation. FC1 CEO Jehad Shona says they are building a development club focused on grassroots football, sustainability and long-term results. Club won their first match 1-0 against Karbi Anglong Morning Star FC.

Article Title: Rock, paper, scissors... then millionaire!: Australian Open brings back Million-Dollar 1 Point Slam
Article Text:
Australia's Jordan Smith holds his trophy aloft after defeating Joanna Garland of Taiwan to win the 1 Point Slam event ahead of the Australian Open in Melbourne, Australia, Jan. 14, 2026. (James Ross/AAP Image via AP, File)

From amateur to millionaire

One point decides everything

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tennis stars , amateurs and celebrities on one court

The Australian Open is bringing back one of its most talked-about innovations after confirming that the Million-Dollar 1 Point Slam will return during the tournament's Opening Week in 2027. Tournament organisers announced on Wednesday that the fan-favourite exhibition event will once again offer a staggering AUD 1 million (approximately USD 705,000) to the winner ahead of the year's first Grand Slam, which runs from January 17 to 31 at Melbourne Park.The announcement follows the overwhelming success of the inaugural edition, where an unknown local amateur stunned some of tennis' biggest names to walk away with a life-changing prize.The debut edition produced one of the most remarkable stories of the 2026 Australian Open. Local amateur Jordan Smith defied the odds by eliminating World No. 1 Jannik Sinner before going all the way to claim the AUD 1 million prize. Smith secured the title after Taiwan's Joanna Garland sent a two-handed backhand wide on just the third shot of the final point, instantly turning the Australian into a millionaire.Unlike conventional tennis tournaments, the 1 Point Slam is built entirely around sudden death.Every match consists of just one point. Before play begins, the two competitors decide the server through a game of rock, paper, scissors. The chosen server gets only one opportunity to put the ball in play. A fault, double fault or let that fails to land legally results in immediate elimination. Once the serve is in, the rally continues until the point is won, with the victor progressing to the next round. The knockout format creates constant jeopardy, ensuring every shot carries enormous significance.One of the biggest attractions of the event is its diverse field. The tournament features professional players, local amateurs and celebrities competing in the same draw. Last year's edition included Grand Slam champions Carlos Alcaraz, Iga Swiatek, Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka and Alexander Zverev, while Taiwanese music superstar Jay Chou also took part.Chou's campaign ended almost instantly after he was knocked out by an ace from Petar Jovic without managing to hit a single ball, a moment that perfectly captured the drama and unpredictability of the format.
Article Summary: The Million-Dollar 1 Point Slam will return during the tournament's Opening Week in 2027. Tournament organisers announced on Wednesday that the fan-favourite exhibition event will once again offer a staggering AUD 1 million (approximately USD 705,000) to the winner. Last year's edition included Grand Slam champions Carlos Alcaraz, Iga Swiatek, Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka and Alexander Zverev. Local amateur Jordan Smith defied the odds by eliminating World No. 1 Jannik Sinner.

Article Title: AICF confirms new dates for chess nationals after GM Abhijeet Gupta flags 2026 snub

NEW DELHI: The All India Chess Federation (AICF) has officially announced new dates for the senior National Chess Championship, ensuring the event is held in 2026 rather than being pushed into 2027. The tournament will now take place from November 29 to December 9, 2026, in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh.The decision follows a social media post by Arjuna Awardee and five-time Commonwealth champion Grandmaster Abhijeet Gupta, who raised serious concerns after the federation initially deferred the 2026 edition to March 2027. As reported by TimesofIndia.com on Monday , the top management at AICF acted quickly as soon as they realised the concerns were genuine. They held immediate meetings with key stakeholders and, understandably, came up with two timeframes for the latter half of 2026.It is reliably learnt that, with those two timeframes, final calls were made with the host state association to see whether the change of plans could be accommodated in Varanasi, as earlier decided. After a long discussion, with the venue unchanged, all parties involved decided to host the tournament in the November-December window.Earlier, the AICF had the event scheduled for March 25 to April 4, 2027. Speaking to TimesofIndia.com, a senior AICF official had previously explained that the shift was forced by a congested international and domestic calendar.It was also conveyed that the federation had prioritised hosting the age-group National Championships early in the year so that players could qualify for the World Championships without running into age-eligibility issues. Since the senior championship has no such age-related deadline, it was kept for later in the calendar.However, GM Abhijeet Gupta took to X (formerly Twitter) to voice strong opposition, pointing out that pushing the tournament to early 2027 effectively meant skipping the 2026 edition entirely.Gupta also highlighted that a March calendar directly conflicted with peak school board exams, forcing young prodigies across the country to choose between their academics and competing for the national title."India is producing world champions, but are we making it harder for the next generation to even compete?" Gupta had posted, urging the AICF to rethink its planning in the best interest of young players.With the scheduling conflict resolved, the focus now shifts back to the board. The upcoming edition in Varanasi will follow the October 2025 championship in Guntur, where Panneerselvam Iniyan edged out Goutham Krishna on a tiebreak to claim his maiden national title.
Article Summary: The All India Chess Federation (AICF) has officially announced new dates for the senior National Chess Championship. The tournament will now take place from November 29 to December 9, 2026, in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh. The decision follows a social media post by Arjuna Awardee and five-time Commonwealth champion Grandmaster Abhijeet Gupta.

Marsh will join the likes of Quinton de Kock, Matthew Breetzke, Jordan Hermann and captain Tristan Stubbs in a powerful batting line-up, set to enthral the loyal St George's Park crowd.Further north, Sam Curran, who represented MI Cape Town in the first two seasons, will don the Durban's Super Giants colours, where he will team up with his England teammate Jos Buttler. Joe Root, England's returning Test captain, who formed a formidable opening partnership with young Lhuan-dre Pretorius for the Paarl Royals a couple of seasons ago, returns to Boland Park for another season in pink.The runners-up, Pretoria Capitals, have received a significant boost to their top order with the additions of Phil Salt and Australian international Matt Short.Salt, who has represented the Capitals previously, will reunite with Short at the top of the order, with the pair currently opening together for Welsh Fire in The Hundred. The duo adds further firepower to a batting line-up featuring Dewald Brevis, Sherfane Rutherford, Andre Russell and last season's breakout star Connor Esterhuizen. England all-rounder Will Jacks, who enjoyed three sensational seasons with the Capitals, has moved down south to Cape Town to complete the trio of MI franchises, being part of the Mumbai Indians in the IPL and currently playing for the MI London setup in The Hundred."Season 5 is shaping up to be our strongest yet," SA20 League Commissioner Graeme Smith said. What excites me most is seeing that quality alongside South Africa's international and domestic stars at the peak of their powers.""The franchises head into the auction with the majority of their squads already locked in, which speaks volumes about the stability and consistency we have built. Among the other prominent releases is England wicketkeeper-batter Jonny Bairstow, who formed a formidable opening partnership with Quinton de Kock for the Sunrisers.MI Cape Town have also parted ways with long-serving players Trent Boult, Rassie van der Dussen and Kieron Pollard, while the likes of Wiaan Mulder and Nandre Burger, who were marquee signings for the Super Kings, will also enter the auction pool.The Super Kings and MI Cape Town will be the busiest teams at the auction, needing to sign seven and six players respectively, while the Capitals have five vacant slots to fill. NEW DELHI: Scottish police are investigating reports that several athletes from Pakistan and Uganda did not return home after the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow ended last Sunday.“Police Scotland has ⁠received reports of several athletes who are unaccounted for,” a spokesperson said late on Tuesday, as quoted by Al Jazeera.“Enquiries are ongoing to assess the circumstances, and early engagement is taking ‌place with the Home Office.”Uganda’s NBS Sport reported that four of its six boxers were missing before the team was due to fly home on Tuesday. One of the athletes reportedly told the broadcaster that they planned to seek asylum. Pakistan Today also reported that one Pakistani boxer did not turn up for the return flight.Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow just hours before the country’s team was scheduled to leave for home. Boxer Fatima Zahra won bronze in the women’s 60kg category, becoming the first Pakistani female boxer to win a Commonwealth Games medal.The result was Pakistan’s lowest medal tally since 1998. Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem also missed out on a medal despite being one of the country’s biggest hopes.

Article Title: WI vs PAK 2nd Test: Babar Azam's wait for Test century continues; Pakistan on brink of victory vs West Indies
Article Text:
Pakistan captain Babar Azam once again missed out on a Test century.

Babar Azam

's wait for Test hundred continues

Warrican leads West Indies bowling attack

Pakistan strikes back with the ball

NEW DELHI: Pakistan moved closer to a rare away Test win after reducing West Indies to 103/6 at stumps on Day 3 of the second and final Test. Despite West Indies holding a lead of 60 runs, the hosts have only four wickets left, giving Pakistan the upper hand heading into the fourth day.West Indies ended the day on 103/6, leading by 60 runs with only four wickets remaining.Pakistan will look to dismiss the remaining batters quickly on Day 4 and chase a modest target to secure their first away Test victory since 2023. West Indies, meanwhile, are aiming to complete a 2-0 series sweep after winning the opening Test by 90 runs.Pakistan began the day still behind West Indies' first-innings total of 344, but Abdullah Shafique produced a superb unbeaten 160 to guide his team to 387.His innings helped Pakistan secure a 43-run first-innings lead before the visitors were bowled out.Left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican starred for West Indies with six wickets for 112 runs. He cleaned up the Pakistan lower order after already removing key batters earlier in the innings.Pakistan captain Babar Azam once again missed out on a Test century.He was run out for 88 after a brilliant direct hit from Brandon King ended his 183-run partnership with Shafique.Pakistan were still trailing by 63 runs when the wicket fell.Babar attempted a quick single after pushing the ball into the off side, but Shafique changed his mind and sent him back. King collected the ball and hit the stumps with a flat throw, leaving Babar short of his ground despite a desperate dive.It was Babar's highest Test score in 35 innings, but he is still waiting for his first Test century since scoring one against New Zealand in Karachi in December 2022.Brandon King's brilliant fielding effort came at a cost.The West Indies batter injured his lower back after landing awkwardly while throwing down the stumps. He had to be taken off the field, and it remains unclear whether he will be able to bat on Day 4.Warrican was the pick of the bowlers for West Indies.He dismissed debutant Awais Zafar for 1 before Shamar Joseph trapped Salman Ali Agha lbw. Warrican then bowled Mohammad Rizwan for 18 with the second new ball and later finished the innings by taking three wickets in four deliveries to complete a six-wicket haul.West Indies made a solid start to their second innings as Tagenarine Chanderpaul and Kavem Hodge added 40 runs for the opening wicket.However, Pakistan's spinners quickly took control.Sajid Khan removed Chanderpaul and Amir Jangoo before West Indies recovered through a partnership between Shai Hope and captain Roston Chase.The visitors then lost three wickets in the final five overs of the day. Sajid trapped Hope lbw for 15 and dismissed Jayden Seales for a two-ball duck. On the last ball of the day, Chase lost his concentration and chipped a simple return catch to Ali Usman after scoring 17.Sajid finished the day with figures of 4/32, while Usman picked up 2/29.
Article Summary: West Indies end the day on 103/6, leading by 60 runs with only four wickets remaining. Abdullah Shafique produced a superb unbeaten 160 to guide his team to 387. Pakistan will look to dismiss the remaining batters quickly on Day 4 and chase a modest target.

Article Title: Babar Azam's Pakistan register first away Test win after three years, beat West Indies by 8 wickets
Article Text:
Babar Azam

Pakistan avoided a series defeat by beating the West Indies by eight wickets in the second Test in Port of Spain on Wednesday. The win ended Pakistan's eight-match losing streak in away Tests and gave them their first Test victory outside home in three years.The two-match series finished 1-1 after the West Indies had won the first Test by 90 runs.It was Pakistan's first away Test win since July 2023, when they defeated Sri Lanka under Babar Azam 's captaincy. Since then, Pakistan went through several changes in coaches, selectors and captains, with Babar stepping down from the role twice. This time, the combination of captain Babar Azam and head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed helped Pakistan return to winning ways overseas.Pakistan chased down the target of 75 runs on the fourth morning, reaching 77/2 shortly after the first session. Abdullah Shafique, who scored a century in the first innings, remained unbeaten on 24, while captain Babar Azam also finished unbeaten on 24.Earlier, Pakistan bowled out the West Indies for 117 in their second innings inside the first half-hour of play on a wearing Queen's Park Oval pitch. Off-spinner Sajid Khan took 4/32 and left-arm spinner Ali Usman claimed 4/39 as the pair shared eight wickets.The West Indies began the day on 106/3 with a lead of 60 runs, but their lower order could not add much. Ali Usman dismissed Kemar Roach and Shamar Joseph, while Justin Greaves, the last recognised batter, added only two runs before playing Mohammad Ali's delivery back onto his stumps while attempting a cross-batted shot.The West Indies were also without opener Brandon King in the second innings. He could not bat because of a back injury suffered on Day 3 when he ran out Babar Azam with a direct hit from short cover.Pakistan's previous away Test win had also come under Babar Azam against Sri Lanka in 2023. During Shan Masood's time as captain, Pakistan lost 3-0 in Australia, 2-0 in South Africa and 2-0 in Bangladesh.Masood was removed as captain after Pakistan's poor run in Test cricket. Babar returned to the role but Pakistan lost the first Test against the West Indies in Tarouba, which became their eighth consecutive away Test defeat before bouncing back in Port of Spain.The victory also changed the standings in the World Test Championship. Pakistan moved up to eighth place with 22.22% of points after two wins and four defeats in six matches. The West Indies dropped to ninth with 20.83% of points after two wins in 12 matches.
Article Summary: Pakistan beat the West Indies by eight wickets in the second Test in Port of Spain. The win ended Pakistan's eight-match losing streak in away Tests and gave them their first Test victory outside home in three years. It was Pakistan's first away Test win since July 2023, when they defeated Sri Lanka under Babar Azam's captaincy.

Article Title: When MS Dhoni stepped away, Virat Kohli-Ravi Shastri toughened up Indian cricket: Ajinkya Rahane
Article Text:
Virat Kohli and Ravi Shastri (Image: X)

'Virat and Ravi toughened up Indian cricket'

Rahane concerned about India's Test mentality

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India vice-captain Ajinkya Rahane believes the appointment of Virat Kohli as Test captain after MS Dhoni's retirement marked a defining moment in Indian cricket, saying Kohli and head coach Ravi Shastri transformed the team's mindset and made it a fearless force, particularly in overseas conditions.Rahane, who recently retired from all forms of cricket, reflected on India's Test evolution during an appearance on the Stick to Cricket podcast alongside Michael Vaughan, Sir Alastair Cook, Phil Tufnell and David "Bumble" Lloyd.When Dhoni retired midway through the 2014-15 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia, Kohli took over the Test captaincy and ushered in an aggressive brand of cricket that helped India become one of the world's strongest travelling teams. Rahane, who was a key member of that era, credited both Kohli and then head coach Ravi Shastri for changing the team's mentality."When MS Dhoni stepped away from Test cricket, Virat Kohli and Ravi Shastri toughened up Indian cricket, especially in overseas Tests. We became more aggressive, bolder, and always proactive rather than defensive," Ajinkya Rahane said in 'stick to cricket'"Virat always told me, 'If you feel like attacking from the very first ball, go for it.He gave players the confidence to play fearlessly," he added.India enjoyed one of its most successful Test periods under Kohli and Shastri, winning historic series in Australia, reaching the summit of the ICC Test rankings and qualifying for the inaugural World Test Championship final.Rahane also expressed concern over the direction of Test cricket, admitting that watching India's recent struggles from the sidelines has been disappointing. Having been out of the Test setup for the past two years before announcing his retirement, the veteran batter said the longest format demands far greater resilience than what is often seen today."Sitting at home because I last two years not been playing Test cricket, watching Indian Test team losing matches even in India as well, I felt Test cricket needs character. You need to build that character. Mental toughness, competitive cricket, that's what is really important.Playing sessions out, " Rahane said.Without naming any particular team, Rahane suggested that modern-day cricketers are increasingly losing the patience required to survive difficult phases of a Test match."Nowadays you don't see many teams, I don't want to pinpoint on anyone, you want to see people playing out those sessions, those tough sessions,'' Rahane concluded.
Article Summary: Former India vice-captain Ajinkya Rahane believes appointment of Virat Kohli as Test captain after MS Dhoni's retirement marked a defining moment in Indian cricket. Rahane, who recently retired from all forms of cricket, reflected on India's Test evolution during an appearance on the Stick to Cricket podcast.

NEW DELHI: Several former Pakistan cricketers could face disciplinary action from the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) after taking part in the Asian Legends League in Zambia without the required approval, according to ESPNcricinfo. More than a dozen retired Pakistan players signed up for the tournament. The controversy began after the Zambia Cricket Union (ZCU), the country's official governing body, said the event was not sanctioned, approved or endorsed by it.The PCB said it has taken "serious notice" of the participation of former Pakistan cricketers in the tournament.Players found to have violated the rules could be banned for two years from receiving a PCB No Objection Certificate (NOC) to participate in approved overseas leagues or cricket events.They could also be declared ineligible for any cricketing, coaching, consultancy, mentoring or other roles with the PCB and the Pakistan Super League (PSL) for two years."In light of the above, the following disciplinary measures will be taken on individuals found to have participated in the said unsanctioned event without obtaining the requisite approvals from the PCB," the PCB statement said. "A ban of two years from the issuance of any PCB No Objection Certificate (NOC) for participation in approved overseas cricket leagues or events.[And] Ineligibility for any cricketing, coaching, consultancy, mentoring and/or other assignments with the PCB and the PSL for a period of two years. "According to ESPNcricinfo, Mohammad Hafeez , Sohail Tanvir and Umar Akmal travelled to Lusaka after signing up for the league. However, they chose not to play after learning that the required ICC approvals had not been received.Several other former Pakistan cricketers are believed to have participated in the tournament.The PCB said all current and former Pakistan cricketers must obtain the required approvals before taking part in overseas cricket events."The PCB remains fully committed to upholding the ICC regulations and safeguarding the integrity and governance of the game," the PCB statement said."The board reiterates that all current and former cricketers seeking to participate in overseas cricket events requiring PCB clearance must obtain the necessary approvals and NOCs prior to participation," it said.

Article Title: Australia gamble on no warm-up games ahead of five-Test Border-Gavaskar Trophy 2027
Article Text:
Australia to skip practice matches ahead of 2027 BGT (Image: ICC)

No practice matches before India tour

Preparations to begin after New Zealand series

Focus on replicating Indian conditions

Test Date Venue 1st Test January 21-25 Vidarbha Cricket Association Stadium, Nagpur 2nd Test January 29-February 2 M. A. Chidambaram Stadium, Chennai 3rd Test February 11-15 Dr. Bhupen Hazarika Cricket Stadium, Guwahati 4th Test February 19-23 JSCA International Stadium Complex, Ranchi 5th Test February 27-March 3 Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad

Australia head coach Andrew McDonald has revealed that his side will not play any practice matches before the 2027 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India, opting instead for an extended training camp tailored to Indian conditions.The five-Test series, scheduled from January 21 to March 3, 2027, marks the first time the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India will be played over five matches after 57 years. The visitors have not won a Test series on Indian soil since the 2004-05 season.Speaking to cricket.com.au about Australia's preparations, McDonald said the team already has sufficient cricket before arriving in India, making traditional tour games unnecessary."We feel as though we've got enough time to immerse ourselves in those conditions. We won't be taking on a practice game. It'll just be more around the location. We've got a couple of options there. We have gone to the UAE previously and we have also gone into India last time into Bangalore, so we're just working through what that would look like in terms of how we then manage the individuals, " McDonald said.Before travelling to India, Australia will play a four-Test home series against New Zealand.McDonald indicated that the squad for India may differ from the one that finishes that series, with selection likely to be based on the specific demands of Indian conditions."A lot of that would happen on the back of the four Tests against New Zealand, seeing where players are at. We'll potentially have some different players with different skill sets that we believe can perform in India, so it won't necessarily be the squad that finishes the Test series (against NZ that then heads to India).There'll be some players that we need to put a little bit more prep into, and that'll start in Australia also, balancing out Big Bash commitments and things like that, " he added.McDonald stressed that Australia's priority is identifying a training base capable of replicating the pitches, weather and overall environment expected during the series opener."Ultimately, if you can have a dedicated venue that you're able to use and replicate as close to the conditions that you believe you may get in the first Test match or throughout a Test series, that's ideally what you want. You case those locations – you want a connection in terms of conditions and climate. We believe we'll get that right in terms of where we go, it just hasn't been confirmed yet, " Head Coach said.Australia have previously held pre-tour camps in the UAE and Bengaluru before touring India, and a similar strategy remains under consideration.
Article Summary: Australia will not play any practice matches before the 2027 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India. The five-Test series, scheduled from January 21 to March 3, 2027, will be played over five matches after 57 years. Australia have not won a Test series on Indian soil since the 2004-05 season.

The Commonwealth Games flag was formally presented to Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel on Wednesday, marking the beginning of preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.After returning from Glasgow, deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi handed over the flag to Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar.Sanghavi had attended the closing ceremony of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Sunday along with Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha. During the ceremony, the Commonwealth Games flag was officially handed over to India as Ahmedabad prepares to host the next edition in 2030.According to an official release, "deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi formally presented the Commonwealth Games Flag, with full honour and dignity, to chief minister Bhupendra Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar."Para-athletes Rakesh Bhatt and Rohit Majgul, who represented Gujarat at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, were present during the ceremony. Para table tennis player Sonal Patel also attended.The release added, "The Commonwealth Games Flag will now remain in Gujarat until the 2030 Commonwealth Games. Along with advancing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Fit India' vision, it will serve as an inspiration for athletes and symbolise the commencement of preparations for the upcoming event."Speaking to reporters after arriving at Ahmedabad Airport earlier in the day, Sanghavi said the city aims to set a new standard for hosting the Commonwealth Games."These Games will be organised with grandeur and with the best possible arrangements for the athletes. They will be conducted in such a way that every athlete can deliver his best performance," the deputy CM said.Sanghavi, who also holds the sports portfolio, said the Gujarat government remains committed to taking forward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Fit India movement and anti-drug campaign."We will advance the anti-drug campaign and the Fit India Movement so that the youth of the country receive maximum opportunities in the sports sector. The Gujarat Government is working towards this goal. Under the guidance of the Government of India, we will continue to move this work forward," he said.
Article Summary: The Commonwealth Games flag was formally presented to Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel on Wednesday. Deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi handed over the flag to Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar. Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha attended the ceremony.

Article Title: Reality check after Commonwealth Games 2026: India’s boxing renaissance to face ultimate Asian exam
Article Text:
New Delhi, Aug 04 (ANI): Union Minister Kiren Rijiju in a group photograph with Indian boxing contingent (@KirenRijiju X/ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. After returning from Glasgow with a historic haul of seven gold and three silver medals, India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.The CWG triumph underlined the country’s growing depth, particularly in women’s boxing. Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) struck gold, while Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg) topped the podium in the men’s competition. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, Jadumani Singh and Narender Berwal added silver medals.The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya, however, will be on an entirely different scale. Unlike the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will feature continental powerhouses such as Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Chinese Taipei, Japan and North Korea — nations that have consistently dominated the World Championships and the Olympics.Uzbek stars Mirazizbek Mirzakhalilov and Bobo-Usmon Baturov, along with Kazakhstan’s Kairat Yeraliyev and Ablaikhan Zhussupov, are expected to headline a field packed with world-class talent.India will also be without two of its Commonwealth champions. Jaismine (57kg) and Arundhati (70kg) will miss out because their weight categories do not feature in the Asian Games programme, depriving the country of two genuine medal prospects.“The Asian Games for us is like the Olympics,” Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh said. “The best teams in the world today are Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and India, and all three are in Asia. Add a strong Chinese contingent and you understand why it is much tougher. You can’t replicate this (CWG) performance at the Asian Games. But if you win a sizeable number of medals at the Asian Games, you can be hopeful of winning medals at the Olympics too.Women’s head coach Santiago Nieva shared a similar assessment while insisting the team remains on the right path.“We can’t guarantee that we will win gold all the time, but we are on the right track. We know how strong the field will be at the Asian Games. The boxers are aware that they can’t sit on their success,” he said.India had returned with one silver and three bronze medals from the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. The Glasgow CWG showcased the strides the boxing contingent has made. But it’ll be Aichi-Nagoya that is going to reveal whether the progress is enough to challenge Asia’s finest and signal genuine medal potential for the 2028 Olympics.
Article Summary: India's record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism. But the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.

Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow, just hours before the country’s Commonwealth Games contingent was scheduled to leave for home.According to a report by Pakistani outlet Geo News, sources in the Pakistan Boxing Federation said Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am. Officials later checked his room and found that he was no longer there.The Pakistan team was due to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before leaving for Pakistan. Article Title: ‘Like preparing for IIT and UPSC together’: Father Murali shares Sreeshankar’s comeback story
Article Text:

KOCHI: S Murali gave an unusual analogy to describe the struggles his son, long jumper Sreeshankar Murali, undertook to regain full fitness after a career-threatening knee injury he sustained two years ago.“Sreeshankar’s comeback was as difficult as preparing for the IIT and Civil Services simultaneously,” he told TOI.Murali is currently near Prague, where he is closely monitoring his son’s training ahead of a busy stretch that begins with the World Athletics Continental Tour (silver level) meet in Bhubaneswar on Aug 22, followed by next month’s Asian Games in Japan.“Sreeshankar’s training now revolves around strength and conditioning, along with the prehab and rehab programme designed by coach Wayne Lombard. There is very little time to work on technique. The priority is to protect the knee on his take-off leg,” Murali said.His IIT-UPSC analogy aptly captures the magnitude of the challenge Sreeshankar faced after suffering the devastating injury just months before the 2024 Paris Olympics.Two years later, the journey came full circle when the 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.“Of all the medals Sreeshankar has won, this one gives me the greatest satisfaction because of the circumstances under which he achieved it. It reflects his mental toughness and hunger,” Murali said.The conditions in Glasgow were anything but favourable.“It was around 12 degrees Celsius with drizzle and strong winds, making the runway tricky,” Murali said. Despite the difficult conditions, Sreeshankar produced a best jump of 8.09m to finish second.The performance inevitably brought back painful memories of 2024, when the family received a grim diagnosis after Sreeshankar tore the patellar tendon in his take-off leg.“The doctors in Mumbai had not seen an injury like this. I thought he would never be able to walk again,” Murali recalled.“They told us it wasn’t a common sports injury but the kind usually seen after a serious car accident. His knee was completely ruptured.”Determined to find the best treatment, Murali travelled nearly 1,900 miles with his son to Doha’s Aspetar Hospital. “The surgeons reconstructed his knee using four screws.”The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process.The painstaking recovery paid rich dividends. Since returning to elite competition, Sreeshankar has consistently cleared the eight-metre mark, including a season’s best of 8.38m at the Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar in June.“There is no time to bask in the Commonwealth Games glory,” Murali said, pointing to the demanding schedule ahead.Sreeshankar will now turn his attention to the Asian Games in Japan, where he hopes to upgrade the silver medal he won at the previous edition in Hangzhou.“With everything Sreeshankar has gone through, he has every reason to believe he can stand on top of the podium at the Asian Games,” Murali concluded.
Article Summary: Sreeshankar Murali suffered a career-threatening knee injury two years ago. The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process. The 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week's Commonwealth Games.
